channel.title: Smart Cities Dive - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Smart Cities Dive (smartcitiesdive.com)

item.title: Teachers struggle to afford housing. What are districts doing about it?
item.description: To help recruit and retain staff, more school districts are stepping in to give them a break on rent — and even a leg up on homeownership.

item.title: Can AI close the language gap in disaster warnings? A federal watchdog raises concerns.
item.description: The National Weather Service lacks clear goals and a funding strategy as it attempts to scale AI-powered multilingual alerts, a Government Accountability Office report warns.

item.title: Frederick County, Maryland, plots a ‘more active’ approach to housing shortages
item.description: The county needs to build nearly 32,000 housing units in the next decade to meet demand, a new report found.

item.title: New bipartisan bill bars major investors from buying single-family homes
item.description: Legislation released in the wake of President Donald Trump’s State of the Union address aims to boost homeownership, but experts say it won’t solve the root problem plaguing housing affordability and access.

item.title: After years of delays, NYC makes $4M bet on modular public toilets
item.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the plan to deliver 20 to 30 new portable, self-cleaning units this year will ensure people can “travel through our city with a little less anxiety.”

item.title: Got a spare room in Portland, Oregon? The city might give you $1K to rent it out.
item.description: The home-sharing program is one of several city efforts to activate "underutilized" housing, Mayor Keith Wilson said.

item.title: Nominate someone today for the 2026 Smart Cities Dive Public Service Awards
item.description: Submit your nominations by March 31 to recognize outstanding local leaders who are making an impact in their communities.

item.title: Brooklyn project shows feasibility of using geothermal in dense urban areas
item.description: Although installation costs are higher than for conventional systems, geothermal is cheaper over the long term, project consultants say.

item.title: APTA calls for $268B investment in public transit and passenger rail over 5 years
item.description: The American Public Transportation Association urges Congress to support transit investment in the upcoming surface transportation legislation.

item.title: 4 ways Oklahoma can ease its affordable housing crisis
item.description: An Urban Institute study detailed challenges in Oklahoma’s housing market but also noted solutions for the state.
